checked_sources: J. Liu, Refinements of the Erdös-Mordell inequality, Barrow's inequality, and Oppenheim's inequality, DOI 10.1186/s13660-015-0947-2, Conjecture 6.3
correctness.rationale: Writing s=sum r_i, T=sum R_i, D=sum r_i R_i-2 sum r_i r_j and E=s(T-2s), direct expansion of Liu's middle term gives the exact identities ((k+2)s/2)(M_k-2s)=E+(k-1)D and (k+2)s(T-M_k)=kE+2(1-k)D. Away from the equilateral center D>0, so with alpha=E/D the two sides reduce exactly to k>=1-alpha and, when alpha<2, k<=2/(2-alpha). For the normalized isosceles side-midpoint boundary family, half-angle parameter u gives alpha(u)=-(u⁴-12u³+4u-1)/(4u³), whose derivative is -(u⁴-8u+3)/(4u⁴). The relevant quartic has a unique minimizer u*=0.377539568391..., yielding alpha*=0.535565054837... and therefore the necessary window 0.464434945162939...<=k<=1.365714473426112.... Continuity transfers strict boundary failure outside this window to genuine interior points. Independent exact/symbolic checks reproduced the derivative and high-precision endpoints.
residual_risks: Finite randomized verification in verification_output.txt is corroborative only; the all-parameter statements are proved analytically.

originality.rationale: Liu's complete open primary article states Conjecture 6.3 exactly on 0.48<=k<=1.36 but does not reduce it to a one-dimensional defect ratio or derive the optimal isosceles boundary obstruction. A later open weighted Erdős-Mordell paper by Tran was read in full enough to compare its main weighted families; they are different coefficient systems and do not state this defect-ratio reduction. Resultary returns the assigned theorem as the exact hit and no prior source with the algebraic endpoints. Plausible later papers listed in the package metadata that were not fully accessible are retained as residual priority risks rather than treated as non-covering evidence.
residual_risks: Full text of several plausible later triangle-inequality papers listed by the package was not independently inspected in this run; accessible indexing/searches did not expose an equivalent defect-ratio theorem.
The isosceles boundary family need not be the globally strongest obstruction.
